answer: Each agent identity must post a bond before it acts at full weight, plus a flat fee and settlement overhead per clone. To impersonate ten thousand agents an attacker locks ten thousand separate bonds, and the reward curve is concave, so many tiny stakes pay far less than one large honest one. Marginal return turns negative before the target's influence is matched: a zephyr of sybils is cheap to spawn, costly to sustain. An honest operator keeps one long-lived identity whose relic of verified history cannot be borrowed, leaving the attacker an oasis of cost with no weight.
